about: Public records about license plate readers in Kern County towns, for /surveillance/<town>/. Every quote is copied from the linked document, word for word, and was read on the 'checked' date. 'units' is the number the record names and 'scope' is the Census place that number is for: the page prints the mapped count for the same place next to it. 'point' is a coordinate the record gives: the page shows the record only when that point is inside one of the town's places. Add a record only after you read the document. Never type a number that the document does not print.

records.doc: application to the Organized Retail Theft Prevention Grant Program
records.source: California Board of State and Community Corrections
quotes: The Tehachapi Police Department is to install 16 Automatic License Plate Readers (ALPR) throughout the city along high traffic areas in and out of our retail and services districts.
Tehachapi has 3 Highway 58 ramps to the north of town, and 2 other two lane roads that take you out of the city.
Additionally, 2 ALPRs will be installed at the primary intersection centered in the business district
records.note: This is an application. The board's summaries of the projects it funded do not name the department.
